tagline: Up the Gulf coast on the old Tamiami Trail.
intro: This stretch of US 41 runs 70 miles up the Gulf side of Florida from the Charlotte County line, through North Port, Venice, Sarasota, Bradenton and Palmetto, to the Hillsborough County line.

It is part of the Tamiami Trail, the road from Tampa to Miami. When the state ran out of construction money for the trail in 1922, the advertising man Barron Collier offered to pay for the rest, and in return the legislature named a county after him. The trail opened on April 26, 1928, after 13 years and 2.6 million sticks of dynamite.

moments.title: Warm Mineral Springs
moments.text: The place is known for a free-flowing artesian spring, and its motel was designed by Victor Lundy, one of the architects of the Sarasota School of Architecture.

moments.title: Venice
moments.text: Fishermen knew the spot as Horse and Chaise for a carriage-shaped stand of trees, and in the 1920s the Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers had John Nolen plan it into a city.

moments.title: Ca' d'Zan
moments.text: John and Mable Ringling's 56-room winter house on Sarasota Bay, finished in 1926, took its Gothic-arched windows from their visits to Venice and its name from the Venetian for House of John.
